payload.description: A high-performance Next.js API that transforms raw GitHub contribution data into premium, 3D isometric monoliths. Featuring real-time GraphQL syncing, custom SVG filters, and deep theme customization

payload.text:
# ⚡ CommitPulse ### _Your GitHub contributions — as a cinematic SVG monolith._ [![Deployed on Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deployed%20on-Vercel-black?style=flat-square&logo=vercel)](https://commitpulse.vercel.app) [![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-16-black?style=flat-square&logo=next.js)](https://nextjs.org) [![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5-3178C6?style=flat-square&logo=typescript)](https://www.typescriptlang.org) [![GraphQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/GraphQL-API-E10098?style=flat-square&logo=graphql)](https://graphql.org) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) --- > **Drop this into your GitHub profile README and stop being boring.** ## 📖 Table of Contents - [Design Philosophy](#the-isometric-monolith--design-philosophy) - [Live Demo](#live-demo) - [Deep Customization](#deep-customization--url-parameters) - [Theme Presets](#theme-presets) - [Theme Preview Gallery](#theme-preview-gallery) - [Real-Time Accuracy](#real-time-accuracy--the-contribution-count-problem) - [Architecture & Tech Stack](#architecture--tech-stack) - [Self-Hosting](#self-hosting-in-4-steps) - [Automated Contributor Workflow](#automated-contributor-workflow) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) - [Themes](#themes) - [Contributors](#contributors) --- ![CommitPulse Live Demo](https://commitpulse.vercel.app/api/streak?user=jhasourav07&theme=neon) [![Join CommitPulse Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join-CommitPulse%20Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/Cb73bS79j) ```md ![CommitPulse](https://commitpulse.vercel.app/api/streak?user=YOUR_USERNAME) ```
--- ## 🏛️ The Isometric Monolith — Design Philosophy Most GitHub stat badges are **flat**. Flat bars, flat text, flat colors. They blend into every README on the planet. **CommitPulse is different.** We render your contribution data as a **3D Isometric City** — a grid of glowing towers where each column's height is directly proportional to your commit count that day. The more you grind, the taller your skyline grows. **Ghost City Architecture:** In this mode, zero-contribution days aren't just empty space. They are rendered as thin, wireframe-style **blueprint foundations** (4px high). This gives your commit landscape a structured, architectural "work-in-progress" look even during rest days, maintaining the premium 3D aesthetic across the entire calendar. This is not decoration. This is a **live, animated data visualization** that makes your dedication impossible to ignore. ### Why Isometric > Flat | Property | Flat Badges | CommitPulse Monolith | | ---------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Visual Depth** | None | Full isometric 3D perspective | | **Data Density** | 3 numbers | 98-day contribution landscape | | **Animation** | Static | Radar scan line, glow effects & live pulsing indicator for today's commits | | **Personality** | Generic | Uniquely yours, every day | | **Impression** | "They have stats" | "They ship code like a machine" | The design philosophy is simple: **your commit history deserves a monument, not a meter.** --- ## 🔴 Live Demo Transform your GitHub contribution history into a cinematic 3D monolith. ### ✨ Theme Showcase
#### Default #### Neon #### Custom
--- ### 📋 Copy Examples #### 🌑 Default ```md ![CommitPulse](https://commitpulse.vercel.app/api/streak?user=jhasourav07) ``` #### 🌟 Neon ```md ![CommitPulse](https://commitpulse.vercel.app/api/streak?user=jhasourav07&theme=neon) ``` #### 🔥 Custom ```md ![CommitPulse](https://commitpulse.vercel.app/api/streak?user=jhasourav07&bg=0a0a0a&accent=ff6b35&text=ffffff) ``` --- ## 🎨 Deep Customization — URL Parameters CommitPulse is designed to be **fully composable**. Every visual attribute is controllable via a URL parameter, following a clear priority chain: ``` URL Parameter > Theme Default > System Fallback ``` ### Parameter Reference | Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description | | ----------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `user` | `string` | ✅ **Yes** | — | GitHub username to render | | `theme` | `string` | No | `dark` | Preset theme name (see below) | | `bg` | `hex` | No | Theme default | Background color — **without** `#` | | `accent` | `hex` | No | Theme default | Tower & glow color — **without** `#` | | `text` | `hex` | No | Theme default | Label & stat text color — **without** `#` | | `radius` | `number` | No | `8` | Border corner radius in pixels | | `border` | `string` | No | — | Custom stroke color around the main SVG container — **without** `#` | | `speed` | `string` | No | `8s` | Radar scan duration (`2s`–`20s`, default `8s`) | | `scale` | `string` | No | `linear` | Tower height scaling: `linear` or `log` (logarithmic) | | `size` | `string` | No | `medium` | Badge dimensions: `small` (400×280), `medium` (600×420), `large` (800×560) | | `font` | `string` | No | CommitPulse default typography | Any **Google Font** name (e.g. `Orbitron`, `Inter`) | | `refresh` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Bypass cache for real-time data | | `year` | `string` | No | — | Calendar year to render (e.g. `2023`, `2024`) | | `hide_title` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Hide GitHub username/title from the SVG badge | | `hide_background` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Remove the background rect, letting the monolith float on the page | | `hide_stats` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Hides the bottom row displaying Current Streak, Annual Sync Total, and Peak Streak stats when set to `true` or `1`. | | `tz` | `string` | No | Omitted = UTC | IANA timezone (e.g. `Asia/Kolkata`, `America/New_York`) — aligns "today" with the user local midnight. Note: `?tz=UTC` is valid but cached separately from omitting `tz`. | | `lang` | `string` | No | `en` | Language code for labels (`en`, `es`, `hi`, `fr`, `pt`, `ko`, `ja`, `de`, `zh`) | | `view` | `string` | No | `default` | Rendering mode: `default` (3D Monolith), `monthly` (Compact monthly stats), or `heatmap` (flat 2D contribution heatmap) | | `entrance` | `string` | No | `rise` | Entrance animation for towers: `rise` (default), `fade`, `slide`, or `none`. | | `delta_format` | `string` | No | `percent` | Format for month-over-month delta in monthly view: `percent` (e.g. +12%), `absolute` (e.g. +15 commits), or `both` | | `width` | `number` | No | `300` | Custom width for the SVG canvas (currently only applies to `view=monthly`) | | `height` | `number` | No | `120` | Custom height for the SVG canvas (currently only applies to `view=monthly`) | | `grace` | `number` | No | `1` | Grace period in days before a streak resets (0–7). `grace=0` = strict mode (no missed days), `grace=2` = lenient (forgives up to 2 missed days). Default is `1`. | | `mode` | `string` | No | `commits` | Rendering mode: `commits` (default) or `loc` (Lines of Code landscape) | | `repo` | `strin

# 🤝 Contributing to CommitPulse > **CommitPulse is built by the open-source community, for the open-source community.** > Whether you're a first-year developer from India shipping your first PR, or a senior engineer with 10 years of SVG experience — you belong here. The only requirement is that you care about quality. --- ## 📋 Table of Contents - [The Standard We Hold](#-the-standard-we-hold) - [Local Setup](#-local-setup) - [Testing & Previewing Your Changes](#-testing--previewing-your-changes) - [What to Contribute](#-what-to-contribute) - [Automated Issue Management & Claiming](#-automated-issue-management--claiming) - [Branch & Commit Conventions](#-branch--commit-conventions) - [Opening a Pull Request](#-opening-a-pull-request) - [Code Style & Quality Gates](#-code-style--quality-gates) - [Community Guidelines](#-community-guidelines) --- ## 🏆 The Standard We Hold CommitPulse is not a generic badge generator. It is a **premium, high-fidelity data visualization tool** with a distinct aesthetic identity. Every contribution must uphold this standard. Before you open a PR, ask yourself: > _"Does this look like something you'd find in a Dribbble showcase or a polished SaaS product — or does it look like a placeholder?"_ **If the answer is the latter, it's not ready yet.** This is not gatekeeping — it's respect for the developers who embed CommitPulse in their public profiles. ### What "Premium Quality" Means in Practice - ✅ SVGs must use curated, harmonious color palettes — not arbitrary hex codes - ✅ Animations must be smooth and purposeful — not distracting or janky - ✅ Typography must match the `Syncopate` / `Space Grotesk` design system - ✅ New themes must feel cohesive — every `bg`, `accent`, and `text` value must work _together_ - ❌ No raw, unstyled `` or `` elements without intentional styling - ❌ No flat, MS-Paint-level color combinations - ❌ No breaking changes to the public API without a migration path --- ## 🛠️ Local Setup Get CommitPulse running on your machine in under 5 minutes. ### Prerequisites - **Node.js** `v18+` - **npm** `v9+` - A **GitHub Personal Access Token** — [generate one here](https://github.com/settings/tokens/new) with the `read:user` scope ### Step-by-Step ```bash # Step 1 — Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/JhaSourav07/commitpulse.git cd commitpulse # Step 2 — Install dependencies npm install # Step 3 — Set up your environment variables from the provided template cp .env.local.example .env.local ``` Open `.env.local` and fill in your values. Every variable is documented inside the file. The key ones are: > **Why is `GITHUB_TOKEN` required?** The GitHub GraphQL API requires authentication. Without a valid `GITHUB_TOKEN`, every request to `/api/streak` will return a `401 Unauthorized` error and the badge will not render. > **Why is `MONGODB_URI` optional?** The `/api/track-user` route is designed to degrade gracefully. If the variable is missing, it logs a warning to the console and skips the DB write — your local dev experience is completely unaffected. **Generating a Personal Access Token (classic):** Go to **GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic)** and click **Generate new token (classic)**. Enable the `read:user` scope, set an expiry, and copy the generated token into your `.env.local`. ```bash # Step 4 — Start the dev server npm run dev ``` Open your browser and test your changes: ``` http://localhost:3000/api/streak?user=YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME ``` > **⚠️ Important:** Never commit your `.env.local` file or expose your `GITHUB_TOKEN`. It is already in `.gitignore`. --- ## 🧪 Testing & Previewing Your Changes Before opening a PR, every contributor is expected to verify their changes locally across three areas: **visual SVG output**, **unit tests**, and **branch coverage**. This section explains how to do all three. ### 1. Visual Browser Preview With your dev server running (`npm run dev`), open your browser and visit these URLs to preview the SVG output directly — **open them as raw URLs, not embedded in an `` tag or Markdown preview**: **Standard badge — valid username:** ``` http://localhost:3000/api/streak?user=YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME ``` **Monthly view:** ``` http://localhost:3000/api/streak?user=YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME&view=monthly ``` **Custom theme — test your color changes:** ``` http://localhost:3000/api/streak?user=YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME&theme=YOUR_THEME_NAME ``` **Invalid username — must render a styled SVG error card, not raw JSON:** ``` http://localhost:3000/api/streak?user=vivek%20Sangani ``` **Non-existent username — must render the ghost-city not-found badge:** ``` http://localhost:3000/api/streak?user=xyzabc999notreallll ``` **Useful DevTools tricks:** - **Inspect SVG structure:** Open DevTools (`Cmd+Option+I` / `F12`) → Elements panel → expand the `

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body: Thanks for the PR, but we cannot merge this. The hash-based selection in isRandomTheme is actually a deliberate design choice! It provides a deterministic pseudo-random theme for a specific username. If we use Math.random(), the SVG badge will flash a completely different theme every single time the user refreshes their GitHub profile, which is a poor user experience and completely defeats HTTP caching. Please close this PR.

payload.author: Vishvadharman
payload.body:
Hi @souravjhahind,

I started implementing #1430 and found that the current codebase intentionally clamps/falls back invalid `grace` values.

Existing tests currently expect:

* `grace=8` → clamps to `7`
* `grace=-1` → clamps to `0`
* non-numeric values → falls back to `1`

When I changed `grace=-1` to return `400 Bad Request`, those existing tests failed.

Should I update the existing tests and change the behavior to strict validation for `grace`, or should I preserve the current clamping behavior and add coverage around that instead?

payload.title: fix(api): mask email in GET /api/notify to prevent PII exposure

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body: ## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. This PR reduces PII exposure by masking email addresses returned from `GET /api/notify`. **Changes:** - Added `maskEmail()` helper to obfuscate email addresses in unauthenticated GET responses. - Updated `GET /api/notify` to return a masked email instead of the raw value. - Added a test asserting that GET responses do not return the full email. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | app/api/notify/route.ts | Introduces `maskEmail()` and applies it to GET responses to avoid returning raw emails. | | app/api/notify/route.test.ts | Adds coverage to ensure GET responses mask emails (PII redaction). | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the PR. The code changes in \lib/cache.ts\ and \lib/github.ts\ for the distributed Redis Mutex lock look excellent and effectively solve the cache stampede vulnerability.

However, this PR includes massive unintended churn in \package-lock.json\ (2783 additions, 692 deletions). Our \package-lock.json\ is highly volatile and we avoid accidental commits of reformatted lock files.

Please revert the \package-lock.json\ file so that only the source code files are included in this PR. Once that is done, I will be happy to approve it!

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the PR @rudra3007-pro.

However, I cannot approve this PR as-is. Mongoose already provides a native mapping for connection states via \mongoose.STATES\ (e.g., \mongoose.STATES[mongoose.connection.readyState]\). Adding a custom utility function to manually map these numeric codes to strings is redundant and reinvents built-in driver functionality. 

Furthermore, we do not currently have a health check endpoint that requires this, making it dead code.

Please close this PR. If you'd like to contribute, please check out open issues that involve fixing actual application logic!

payload.author: Tranquil666
payload.title: fix: apply grace parameter to longest streak calculation

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the PR @Tranquil666.

However, I cannot approve this change because it relies on a fundamental misunderstanding of what the grace parameter does. 

The grace parameter is not a historical hole-puncher for missing days. It exists solely to provide timezone/delay tolerance for the *current edge of the timeline* (e.g., if it is morning in your timezone and you haven't committed yet today, grace=1 prevents your current streak from dropping to 0 by tolerating a 0 on the *current* day).

If you look closely at the currentStreak calculation in lib/calculate.ts, you'll see that it **does not** tolerate 0-contribution days in the middle of a streak—it only tolerates them at the very end (i >= todayIndex - grace). 

If we apply this PR's logic to longestStreak, it will allow users to bridge 1-day gaps anywhere in their history infinitely. A user could commit every other day for a year and this PR would calculate that as a 365-day streak. That completely breaks the definition of a consecutive streak.

Please close this PR as the current logic is actually correct!

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. Adds validation, rate limiting, and graceful MONGODB_URI handling to the `/api/notify` endpoint, replacing manual checks with Zod schemas and integrating the endpoint with the global middleware rate limiter. **Changes:** - Introduces `notifyPostSchema` and `notifyGetSchema` Zod validators and exports `GITHUB_USERNAME_REGEX`. - Refactors `POST`/`GET` in `app/api/notify/route.ts` to use Zod validation, per-route rate limiting, and dev-friendly bypass when `MONGODB_URI` is missing. - Adds the `/api/notify` route to the middleware matcher and expands tests for new behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | middleware.ts | Adds `/api/notify` to the rate-limit middleware matcher and docstring. | | lib/validations.ts | Exports the GitHub username regex and adds Zod schemas/types for notify POST/GET. | | lib/rate-limit.ts | Adds a dedicated `notifyRateLimiter` instance (5 req/min/IP). | | app/api/notify/route.ts | Replaces manual validation with Zod, adds rate limiting, safe JSON parsing, and graceful MONGODB_URI handling. | | app/api/notify/route.test.ts | Adds tests for validation, rate-limiting, MONGODB_URI behavior, and success paths. |

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the PR @kanishka-2007-tech.

However, I cannot approve this PR as-is. 
1. Just like in your previous PRs, you inadvertently reformatted \package-lock.json\ with over 1400 lines of changes.
2. We do not accept tests that verify Mongoose's internal connection state behaviors (such as state 99 lazy initialization). Mongoose's own unit test suite is responsible for testing database driver states. We only write tests for our own application's business logic.

Please close this PR. If you'd like to contribute, please check out open issues that involve fixing actual application logic!

Thanks for the contribution @ThePriyanuj.

However, I cannot approve this PR as-is. Both of the tests you added are exact duplicates of test coverage that already exists on the \main\ branch!

1. In \lib/validations.test.ts\, we already have \it('should reject user values longer than 39 characters')\ and \it('should fail when user exceeds 39 characters')\ which perform the exact same \'a'.repeat(40)\ check.
2. In \app/api/streak/route.test.ts\, the test literally right above the one you added already asserts that the endpoint returns a 400 with 'cannot exceed 39 characters'.

We do not accept redundant test suites that merely duplicate existing validation coverage. Please close this PR. If you'd like to contribute, please check out open issues that involve fixing actual application logic!

payload.author: Kokila-chandrakar
payload.title: improve: enhance contributors loading state accessibility and feedback

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the contribution @Kokila-chandrakar! The addition of role="status" and aria-live="polite" is a great accessibility improvement for the loading state. However, you added an `sr-only` span with the exact same text as the already visible paragraph: ```tsx

Loading contributors...

... Loading contributors ``` Because both are inside the `aria-live` region, a screen reader will redundantly announce "Loading contributors" twice. The `sr-only` class is meant to provide screen-reader text when there is NO visible text (for example, on an icon-only button or a spinner that has no label). Since the loading message is already visible text on the screen, it does not need a hidden duplicate. Please remove the `Loading contributors` element. Once that is fixed, I would be happy to approve this!

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body: The loading spinner already existed on `main`, so this PR isn't really adding a loading state — it's just adding `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` to it plus a second line of text. The PR description oversells it and falsely claims an `sr-only` element that doesn't exist in the diff. Squash the 2 commits into 1, fix the description to say "accessibility enhancement" instead of "new loading state", and clarify whether #2010 was already solved before this PR.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the contribution @ThePriyanuj.

However, I cannot approve this PR as-is. While these tests are very thorough, they are exclusively testing Mongoose's internal mechanisms (such as verifying that \User.collection.queue\ buffers operations correctly when \eadyState\ is 2). This is exactly what the Mongoose library's own unit test suite is responsible for testing. 

We should only write tests for our own application's business logic, not for the internal behaviors of our third-party dependencies. Please close this PR, or pivot to testing an actually untested piece of application logic!

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the contribution @ThePriyanuj. 

However, I cannot approve this PR as-is. The \main\ branch already contains test coverage for connection state 0 in \models/User.test.ts\ under the \Database Connection State 0 Handling\ block. 

Furthermore, writing explicit tests to assert that Mongoose delegates \ indOne\ or \updateOne\ to its underlying MongoDB driver collection when \eadyState === 1\ is testing Mongoose's internal library implementation details, not our application's logic. These tests do not add meaningful value to our codebase and only introduce maintenance overhead.

Please either pivot this PR to test actual untested application logic, or close it if there are no new application behaviors to test here.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the PR @AnushKamble! It looks like there's a disconnect between the PR title/description and the actual code changes.

**Issue: Missing Implementation**
Your PR description explains that you're adding pagination with \weeks(first: 54)\ and reducing \maxRepositories\ from 100 to 50 for the GraphQL query fetching 3D monolith data. 

However, looking at the code diff, none of those changes are included. The only changes in this PR are:
1. Adding the \server-only\ package to \package.json\ (and \package-lock.json\)
2. Importing \server-only\ into \lib/github.ts\
3. Mocking \server-only\ in \lib/github.test.ts\

While adding \server-only\ to backend utility files is a great practice to prevent accidental client-side data leaks, it doesn't solve the GraphQL exhaustion issue described in the PR. Please push the actual GraphQL query updates (and feel free to keep the \server-only\ improvement as well!).

Looking forward to reviewing the updated code once you push the missing changes.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the PR @AnushKamble!

Unlike PR #2023, the description here perfectly matches the code changes! Adding \server-only\ to \lib/github.ts\ is an excellent security measure to ensure our GitHub tokens can never accidentally leak into the client bundle.

However, there is one issue: you accidentally committed a massive change to \package-lock.json\ (over 2000 lines added/modified). This usually happens when running \
pm install\ locally with a different Node/npm version than what the project expects, which reformats the entire lockfile. 

Also, it looks like the Vitest suite fails to resolve the \server-only\ import during CI. 

Please revert the \package-lock.json\ changes using \git checkout origin/main -- package-lock.json\, and then re-install just the specific package using \
pm install server-only\ to keep the diff minimal. Once the lockfile is clean and the CI tests pass, I'll be happy to approve this!

payload.author: bhoomisingh00079
payload.title: test(mongodb): verify User schema behaviors under connection state 3 (disconnecting) (Variation 3)

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the contribution @bhoomisingh00079! Unfortunately this PR cannot be merged as-is due to two critical issues.

**Issue 1 — Removes existing test coverage in lib/mongodb.test.ts**
The PR deletes the handles mongoose Connection State 0 (disconnected) gracefully test and replaces it with a state 3 test. However, main already has **two** state 3 tests in lib/mongodb.test.ts:
- handles mongoose Connection State 3 (disconnecting) gracefully (success path)
- handles mongoose Connection State 3 (disconnecting) gracefully by throwing or clearing cache (failure path)

By deleting the state 0 test, this PR removes coverage for the disconnected error path — a net regression.

**Issue 2 — Removes existing test coverage in models/User.test.ts**
The PR deletes the Database Connection State 2 Handling block and replaces it with a state 3 test. But main already has Database Connection State 3 (Disconnecting) Handling (which tests transaction abort behaviour). Adding another state 3 test here while removing state 2 is again a net regression.

**What you should do to fix this:**
1. **Do not delete any existing tests** — only add new ones.
2. Check what is already covered in the target file before writing your test.
3. Since state 0, 2, and 3 are already covered in both files, consider covering a genuinely untested scenario — for example, state 1 (connected) edge cases, concurrent connection attempts, or MONGODB_URI validation under different states.

The overall test count stayed at 1289 (same as main), confirming no new coverage was added. Happy to approve once the PR adds tests without removing any existing ones.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body: Both test files have copy-pasted duplicate blocks the state 3 test appears twice in `mongodb.test.ts` and the entire state 3 `describe` block is duplicated in `User.test.ts`. There's also a dead `mockMongoose` variable sitting unused in the state 0 test. Beyond the duplicates, the state 3 transaction test doesn't actually test any app code — it defines a function inline and then tests that function, which is just verifying its own mock. The original state 2 test was also silently replaced with a weaker version. Fix: remove duplicates, delete the dead variable, squash the 2 commits (first one has a typo too), and ideally rewrite the state 3 test to verify real application behavior.

payload.title: https://github.com/Brightfringe/commitpulse/pull/new/fix/consolidate-rate-limiter

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
@Brightfringe
  - Architectural Regression: They completely removed DistributedCache from the rate limiter. This breaks global Redis rate-limiting on Vercel KV/Upstash, converting it to a per-instance limit that attackers can easily bypass by hitting different edge nodes.
- Logic Bug (Sliding Window Bug): The reset time returned by the wrapper is incorrectly calculated as Date.now() + windowMs dynamically on every request. This causes the X- - RateLimit-Reset header to tell clients a fake, shifting reset time that forces them to back off longer than the server actually requires.
- Missing TTLCache Expiration Exposer: The underlying TTLCache currently doesn't expose a method to get the true expiration time of a key, which is needed to fix the bug above.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for the contribution @boss477. However, I cannot approve this PR as-is.

**Issue: Exact Duplicate Integration Test**
In `app/api/streak/route.test.ts`, you added the following test:
```typescript
it('returns 400 when an invalid ISO8601 calendar date format like "2026-15-40" is supplied (Variation 4)'
```
This test **already exists** right above it on line 650 (`returns 400 when an invalid ISO8601 calendar date format like "2026-15-40" is supplied`). Adding an identical test with `(Variation 4)` appended to the title does not add any new test coverage. Please delete this duplicate test.

The unit tests added in `lib/validations.test.ts` are fine since the `date` parameter lacked explicit schema-level coverage there, but the duplicate route test must be removed before this can be merged.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Code looks correct — adds `layout` validation via `z.refine()` that rejects unsupported values with 400 instead of silently falling back, with unit tests (valid/invalid) and updated route tests. 220/220 tests pass.

However, this PR has the `needs-rebase` label — the `streakParamsSchema` has been restructured into `baseStreakParamsSchema` in recent merges (e.g., the `glow` feature), so this branch will likely conflict. Note that this is also a **breaking change**: existing API consumers passing unknown `?layout=` values will now get 400 instead of the previous silent fallback to `'default'`.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Issue 1 — Duplicate tests in lib/validations.test.ts

The main branch already contains the exact same 6 layout validation tests twice — two identical Variation 2 blocks at lines 886–946 and 952–1012. This PR adds them a third time as Variation 4 with the same inputs (unsupported_layout, default, compact, full, omitted) and identical assertions, which adds zero new coverage.

How to fix: Either remove the 6 validation tests entirely since they're already covered, or replace them with genuinely new scenarios such as:
- Empty string: layout: ''
- Whitespace: layout: ' '
- Case sensitivity: layout: 'Default' or layout: 'COMPACT'

Issue 2 — Removed assertion in app/api/streak/route.test.ts

The existing test returns 400 when ?layout= is invalid previously had this assertion which your diff deletes:

expect(body.details).not.toBeNull();

Please restore it. The new test you added alongside it is welcome and should stay — just don't remove the existing assertion.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
The two new tests do not deliver the value claimed in the PR description:

1. `supports screen reader operations by using semantic HTML`: Falls back to `container.querySelector('div')` — every component has a `div` wrapper, so this is a no-op assertion. A meaningful accessibility test should check for `role`, `aria-*`, or semantic element assertions without fallbacks.

2. `adapts layouts correctly across mobile and desktop viewports`: Renders the same component twice with no viewport/media-query change. The test does not actually verify responsive behavior. To test responsiveness, consider using a utility like `window.resizeTo` or checking that breakpoint-specific classes render correctly.

Please revise these tests to actually validate the claimed properties (accessibility semantics and responsive layout adaptation).

payload.author: Apurva-Lakhe
payload.body:
Hi @Aamod007  I've updated both tests to make sure they validate structural value properly:

1. **Accessibility Semantics:** Replaced the generic fallback container queries with a strict `screen.getByRole('contentinfo')` assertion. This explicitly verifies that the element renders a semantic `<footer />` landmark structure that is exposed to assistive technologies.
2. **Responsive Layouts:** Since JSDOM does not natively parse CSS media queries to trigger layout-engine shifts, I updated the responsiveness test to explicitly assert that structural rendering properties and responsive utility breakpoint mappings (like flex settings and device classes) are hardcoded directly within the DOM.

All 6 tests are fully passing locally and the changes have been cleanly pushed up to the tracking branch!

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. Adds a new optional `glow` parameter to streak/heatmap badges, allowing users to disable SVG glow filters via query string. Defaults to `true` to preserve current behavior. **Changes:** - Adds `glow` field to `BadgeParams` type and `streakParamsSchema` with default `true`. - Conditionally renders `` / `` defs and `filter="url(...)"` attributes in `generator.ts` based on `params.glow`. - Threads `glow` through the streak API route and adds unit tests for schema and SVG rendering. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | types/index.ts | Adds optional `glow` field to `BadgeParams`. | | lib/validations.ts | Adds `glow` zod field with default `true` and string→boolean transform. | | lib/validations.test.ts | Tests for the new `glow` schema behavior. | | lib/svg/generator.ts | Conditionally emits glow filters and attributes; plumbs `glow` into heatmap grid. | | lib/svg/generator.test.ts | Tests glow inclusion/omission in main and heatmap SVGs. | | app/api/streak/route.ts | Extracts and forwards `glow` into badge params. |
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Adds a `glow` URL parameter (defaults to `true`, backward compatible) to toggle heavy SVG Gaussian blur filters. When `glow=false`, the `<filter id=glow>` (and `hm-glow` for heatmaps) tags are omitted from `<defs>`, and `filter=url(#glow)` attributes are removed from text/cell elements. Applied across regular badge SVG, wrapped SVG, heatmap SVG, and auto-theme heatmap variants.

- 6 files, +147/-21
- 1158/1158 tests pass (4 pre-existing failures from missing `gsap`/`react-force-graph-2d` deps)
- TypeScript typecheck has no new errors

👋 Hey @boss477, welcome to **CommitPulse**! 🎉

Thanks for opening your first pull request — this is a big deal and we appreciate the effort!

While you wait for a review, please double-check:
- ✅ You've read the [**CONTRIBUTING.md**](https://github.com/JhaSourav07/commitpulse/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) checklist
- ✅ `npm run lint`, `npm run format`, and `npm run test` all pass locally
- ✅ Your PR has a visual preview if it touches any SVG output
- 💬 You've joined our [**Discord**](https://discord.gg/Cb73bS79j) for faster PR feedback

A maintainer will review your PR shortly. Hang tight! 🚀

👋 Hey @boss477, it looks like you didn't use our PR template!

The section **`## Description`** is missing from your PR description.

Please update your PR description to include all required sections so we can review this properly:
- **`## Description`** — What does this PR do? Which issue does it fix?
- **`## Pillar`** — Which contribution pillar does this fall under?
- **`## Checklist`** — Have you ticked off the quality checklist?

You can find the full template in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/JhaSourav07/commitpulse/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-opening-a-pull-request). Just edit your PR description and the `needs-details` label will be removed automatically. 🙌
